title: Planner: AI-generated status reports in Planner Agent
summary: The rollout, licence requirements and printed controls are supported by the supplied records and Microsoft documentation. One qualification needs narrowing: Learn explicitly covers status reporting in Planner under the PowerShell control, while directing administrators elsewhere for Planner Agent in Microsoft Copilot.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not specified whether this report is created under an identity other than the requesting user's.
claims.quote: Searched: "Planner Agent" "status reports" "identity"; read MC1506735 and learn.microsoft.com/planner/turn-off-planner-agent. Neither specifies the report-creation identity; search results about other agents do not establish it.

claims.claim: Nothing in the supplied notice describes the agent sending a report autonomously.
claims.quote: Searched: sending and autonomy in the complete supplied MC1506735 post; it describes an authorized user's request, review, refinement and optional export, not autonomous sending.

claims.claim: No admin UI equivalent is documented for the Planner-specific all-users or security-group PowerShell setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "Planner Agent" "status reports" "admin center" "restrict"; opened learn.microsoft.com/planner/turn-off-planner-agent. It documents PowerShell; the surfaced Planner Plugin and Copilot agent UI controls are different surfaces.

claims.claim: Planner policy changes can take up to one hour to become effective.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Planner PowerShell setting controls Planner Agent access for all users or a security group, including status reporting in Planner.
claims.quote: This article contains instructions for how to restrict access to the Planner Agent experience for task execution and status reporting in both basic and premium plans

claims.claim: The correctly documented Planner control is presented with a caveat that applicability to the new AI-generated reports remains unconfirmed.
claims.quote: restrict access to the Planner Agent experience for task execution and status reporting in both basic and premium plans ... For information on how to manage the Planner Agent in Microsoft Copilot, please see Manage agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.fix: Replace the applicability caveat in controls[1].note and the matching prose with: 'Applies to Planner Agent task execution and status reporting in basic and premium plans in Planner. For Planner Agent in Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft directs administrators to the Microsoft 365 admin center.' Narrow the matching open question to whether this Planner-specific setting also governs reports requested in Microsoft Copilot. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/planner/turn-off-planner-agent

claims.claim: The cited agent actions and block API pages do not name Planner Agent specifically.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner across the fetched learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-actions text; no match. Read learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/package/copilotpackage-block in full; no Planner-specific passage.

claims.claim: Disabling Loop affects other Planner experiences in addition to status reports.
claims.quote: When Loop is disabled, users cannot create Loop task lists, so no tasks sync into Planner from them. Tasks users create directly in Planner are not affected.

claims.claim: When auditing is enabled, Copilot user interactions are logged in Microsoft Purview Audit.
claims.quote: If your organization enables auditing, you don't need to take extra steps to configure auditing support for Copilot and AI applications. ... The system automatically generates audit logs when a user interacts with Copilot, Cowork, or an AI application.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends reviewing Planner Agent and Copilot agent availability and settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
